## Assert what the user sees or can do, never internal state or markup

_medium · any_

**Rule.** Assert on what a user or assistive technology perceives: visible text, values, enabled or disabled
state, focus, ARIA attributes, and the calls a callback received. Leave internal state, class names
that carry no meaning for the user, and markup snapshots out of assertions.

**Why.** Tests that read internals break on every refactor that changes nothing for the user, and still pass
when the user-facing behaviour is broken, so the suite stops being trusted.

## Derive the expected value from the test's own input, not a repeated literal

_medium · any_

**Rule.** When the expected value follows from the test's input, compute it from that input: the row count
from the list the test rendered, a field's value from the value the test prefilled. Write a literal
only for a value the test introduces in the assertion itself.

**Why.** A hard-coded copy of the input goes stale the moment the input changes, so the test fails for a
reason unrelated to the code, or keeps passing against the wrong number.

## Group assertions by category, not one test per element

_medium · typescript, storybook@>=10_

**Rule.** Per story state, write one test for the static content, one for accessibility (roles, names,
focus), and one per distinct interaction, validation rule or callback. Wrap a test in `step()` when
it has three or more phases.

**Why.** A test per text node multiplies runtime and noise without catching anything the grouped test
would miss. Grouping by category keeps a failure specific enough to point at the cause.

**Incorrect:**

```ts
Story.test("Shows title", async ({ canvas }) => { await expect(canvas.getByText("Profile")).toBeVisible(); });
Story.test("Shows email", async ({ canvas }) => { await expect(canvas.getByText("a@b.co")).toBeVisible(); });
```

**Correct:**

```ts
Story.test("Renders all expected content", async ({ canvas }) => {
  await expect(canvas.getByRole("heading", { name: "Profile" })).toBeVisible();
  await expect(canvas.getByText("a@b.co")).toBeVisible();
});
```

## Make a separate story only for a different state, not for a different test

_medium · typescript, storybook@>=10_

**Rule.** Create a story for each state the component can render, defined by its args or mocks. When two checks
need the same args, attach both as tests to one story. Interaction, keyboard and accessibility are
tests on these stories, never stories of their own.

**Why.** A story per check fills the sidebar and the docs with copies of one state, and the copies drift apart
when only some of them get the next prop change.

**Incorrect:**

```ts
export const SubmitClick = meta.story({ args: { defaultValues: filled } });
export const SubmitKeyboard = meta.story({ args: { defaultValues: filled } });
```

**Correct:**

```ts
export const FilledForm = meta.story({ args: { defaultValues: filled } });

FilledForm.test("Clicking submit calls onSubmit", async ({ canvas, userEvent, args }) => {});
FilledForm.test("Enter submits the form", async ({ canvas, userEvent, args }) => {});
```

## Give a purely presentational component stories, not invented tests

_medium · typescript, storybook@>=10_

**Rule.** For a component that only renders its props (a card, a badge, an avatar), write one story per
visual variant and no `.test()`. Add a test as soon as the component has behaviour: a callback, a
conditional branch, a keyboard interaction or an ARIA state.

**Why.** A test that re-reads the text a story was given checks the args, not the component, and doubles the
upkeep of every copy change without ever catching a bug.

**Incorrect:**

```ts
export const SuccessBadge = meta.story({ args: { intent: "success", label: "Paid" } });
SuccessBadge.test("Renders the label", async ({ canvas }) => {
  await expect(canvas.getByText("Paid")).toBeVisible();
});
```

**Correct:**

```ts
export const SuccessBadge = meta.story({ args: { intent: "success", label: "Paid" } });
export const WarningBadge = meta.story({ args: { intent: "warning", label: "Overdue" } });
```

## Derive a story variant with Story.extend instead of copying its config

_low · typescript, storybook@>=10_

**Rule.** When a story differs from another only in a few args or parameters, derive it with
`Story.extend({ args: { ... } })` and set only what differs. Keep shared defaults in `meta.args`.

**Why.** A copied story config drifts from its original on the next change, and the reader has to diff two
blocks to see what makes the variant different.

**Incorrect:**

```ts
export const FilledForm = meta.story({ args: { defaultValues: filled, layout: "wide" } });
export const FilledDisabled = meta.story({ args: { defaultValues: filled, layout: "wide", disabled: true } });
```

**Correct:**

```ts
export const FilledForm = meta.story({ args: { defaultValues: filled, layout: "wide" } });
export const FilledDisabled = FilledForm.extend({ args: { disabled: true } });
```

## Label the phases of a long story test with step(), and only of a long one

_low · typescript, storybook@>=10_

**Rule.** When a story test or a `play` function has three or more phases, wrap each one in
`await step("<phase>", async () => { ... })`, taking `step` from the test function's parameters.
Keep tests of one or two lines without `step()`.

**Why.** Comments do not show in the test output, so a failure in a long flat test points at a line number
instead of the phase that broke; wrapping a two-line test adds nesting and says nothing.

**Incorrect:**

```ts
FormStory.test("Submits valid data", async ({ canvas, userEvent, args }) => {
  // fill
  await userEvent.type(canvas.getByLabelText(/email/i), "ada@example.com");
  // submit
  await userEvent.click(canvas.getByRole("button", { name: /sign in/i }));
  // verify
  await expect(args.onSubmit).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
});
```

**Correct:**

```ts
FormStory.test("Submits valid data", async ({ canvas, userEvent, args, step }) => {
  await step("Fill the form", async () => {
    await userEvent.type(canvas.getByLabelText(/email/i), "ada@example.com");
  });
  await step("Submit", async () => {
    await userEvent.click(canvas.getByRole("button", { name: /sign in/i }));
  });
  await step("Verify", async () => {
    await expect(args.onSubmit).toHaveBeenCalledOnce();
  });
});
```

## Name stories after component states and tests after behaviours

_low · typescript, storybook@>=10_

**Rule.** Name each story after the state it shows, as a bare state name (`EmptyForm`, `FilledForm`,
`Loading`); add a `State` suffix only where the bare name would shadow a global (`ErrorState`). A
component with a single story gets `<Component>Story` plus a `name:` field, so it does not collide
with the imported component. Never name a story after a behaviour (`ClickTest`): that is a test. Name each test as a sentence describing one behaviour. Write titles
as space-separated words grouped by area (`"Components/Country Select"`,
`"Features/Invoices/Invoice Table"`), following the grouping the project's stories already use.

**Why.** Generic names say nothing in the sidebar or in a failing CI line. A failing test called "Shows
validation error on empty submit" tells the reader what broke without opening the file.

**Incorrect:**

```ts
export const Default = meta.story({});
Default.test("Test 1", async ({ canvas }) => {});
```

**Correct:**

```ts
export const SubmitButtonStory = meta.story({ name: "Submit Button" });
SubmitButtonStory.test("Disabled button prevents submission", async ({ canvas }) => {});
```
